CS is basically math, and as big as AI, machine learning, and cryptography are, they are only minor fields in CS. Algorithms, data structures, static analysis, performance analysis, grammar, network architecture, compilers, computability, computer architecture, etc. That's not even mentioning the tangential stuff, like math modeling, simulations, graphics, data visualizations, computer-human interaction, animation, .... These often involve computers, but are more about another field of study than computer science itself. Then, there are the tools of the trade. You use them while studying, sure, but none of those things I mentioned above actually need them. These are the particular programming languages, libraries, platforms, APIs, and frameworks. You know, actual software. Being good with these is a whole other beast from being fluent with the fields of study that they support.
